subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Dentistry
description: Foundations in dentistry, including an overview of the history, practice and fundamental concepts in the field of dentistry, oral biology, common pathologies in dentistry, dental public health, patient management and infection control.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 111J2 and DENT 111J3.
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 111J1, DENT 111J2 and DENT 111J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Medicine and Manifestation of Systemic Diseases
description: Fundamental principles in oral medicine and their significance in dental practice, with an emphasis on diagnosis, management and treatment modalities are presented with a focus on the recognition and interpretation of oral manifestations of systemic diseases.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

subject: DENT
title: Community Oral Health Services 1
description: Introduction to the Oral Health Community Services Program. Understanding how to reduce disparities in access to oral health care services by underserved and underprivileged people. Enhance understanding of the inter-relationship between oral and general health.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

subject: DENT
title: Head and Neck Anatomy and Histology
description: Head and neck anatomy including the essential aspects of dissection, histology, pain pathways, and development. The structures, functions, and comprehensive study of the clinical implications related to the head and neck region.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 114D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 114D1 and DENT 114D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Health Research 1
description: Introduction to health research with a focus on oral health research. Overview of research fundamentals through exposure to research activities at the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Exploring why research is important for clinical training.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

subject: DENT
title: Social Justice Seminar 1
description: Introduction to social justice, equity, diversity, harm reduction, social-dynamics involved in the profession. Guided self-reflection, small group workshops, and placing dentistry within greater social context.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 201; D.M.D. students only.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Infection Prevention and Control
description: The use of routine infection control practices in dentistry, implementing practices aimed at preventing crosscontamination of the dental operatory, laboratory, shared clinic supplies, equipment and surfaces.

restrictions.text: Open only to DMD II students

notes: Students must register for both DENT 208D1 and DENT 208D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 208D1 and DENT 208D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Oral Medicine and Oral Diagnosis
description: Introduction to oral diagnosis and oral medicine of dentistry. Didactic component includes history taking, patient’s workup, differential diagnosis, and treatment planning.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

subject: DENT
title: Community Oral Health Services 2
description: Introduction to the Oral Health Community Services Program. Understanding how to reduce disparities in access to oral health care services by underserved and underprivileged people. Enhance understanding of the inter-relationship between oral and general health.

subject: DENT
title: Tooth Movement
description: Introduction to the basic concepts of Orthodontics and management of malocclusions with extensive laboratory and clinical activities.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 215D1 and DENT 215D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 215D1 and DENT 215D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Foundations of Dentistry
description: Introduction of the head and neck anatomy, growth, development of the oral-facial complex, and glands. It also deals with the basic sciences of pain, hard tissues, cariology, and infection control. Extensive head and neck anatomy laboratory work.
notes: Open to DMD students only.

subject: DENT
title: Support Tissue
description: Introduction to the normal and diseased pathways of periodontal structures. Clinical exercises on how to assess periodontal health.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 218D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 218D1 and DENT 218D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Restorative Dentistry
description: Introduction to pre-clinical dental activities including training in restorative dentistry, fixed prosthodontics and operative dentistry. Extensive laboratory work in a pre-clinical dental setting is involved.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 220D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 220D1 and DENT 220D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Tooth Loss
description: Introduction to the concept of edentulism, including both partial and complete restorative solutions for edentulous spaces within the oral cavity. Extensive laboratory and clinical components are involved.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 221D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 221D1 and DENT 221D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Radiology
description: Physics and biologic effects of radiation, radiation protection, imaging principles and techniques and radiographic interpretation of caries, periodontal and periapical disease.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D students only.

subject: DENT
title: Transition to Clinic
description: Introduction to the clinical environment following preclinical work, including the implementation of theoretical knowledge of different areas of dentistry while addressing patient care, infection control, and anesthetics needs.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 224D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 224D1 and DENT 224D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Health Research 2
description: Developing familiarity with oral health research, from research design to hands on experience in conducting research with relevance to clinical dental training.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

subject: DENT
title: Professional Identity Development
description: Exploration of personal and professional identity and stance toward health inequality and inequity, social justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are presented with a consideration of the challenges and opportunities of interpersonal and interprofessional relations.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 206.

subject: DENT
title: Dental Public Health A
description: Introduction to oral health, including various themes in dental care, such as: sustainable dentistry, social dentistry, patient centered care and public health.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 305D1/D2.

subject: DENT
title: Dental Anatomy and Occlusion
description: Introduction to dental anatomy and occlusion, including tooth anatomy, occlusal principles and relationships, and their impact on oral health.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 101 or DENT 220.

subject: DENT
title: Cariology
description: Fundamental, evidence-based knowledge in cariology, including carious lesion diagnosis from early stages, caries risk assessment, non-surgical and surgical caries management through minimal intervention approaches.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 101J1/J2/J3, DENT 217, or DENT 224D1/D2.

subject: DENT
title: Restorative Dentistry (Operative)
description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts of operative dentistry, including psychomotor skills development, tooth preparation for direct restorations, as well as concepts in biomaterial science and their clinical application.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 220D1/D2.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 242J2 and DENT 242J3.
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 242J1, DENT 242J2 and DENT 242J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Endodontics A
description: Fundamental concepts of endodontic therapy and its rationale are presented with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 311J1/J2/J3.

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry A
description: The fundamental concepts of pediatric dentistry are presented including the prevention and management of oral disease in children, and basic restorative procedures, with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 316D1/D2.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 244D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 244D1 and DENT 244D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Restorative Dentistry (Fixed Prosthodontics)
description: Fundamental concepts of extra-coronal restorations are presented including tooth preparation for indirect restorations as well as concepts in biomaterial science and their clinical application, with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 220D1/D2.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 245D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 245D1 and DENT 245D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Management of Partial Edentulism
description: Fundamental concepts of removable prosthodontics for the partially edentulous patient are presented with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development in a simulated environment, including partial edentulism and the treatment strategies recommended.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 221D1/D2.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 246D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 246D1 and DENT 246D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Management of Complete Edentulism
description: Fundamental concepts of removable prosthodontics for the complete edentulous patient with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development in a simulated environment are presented including complete edentulism, its impact on patients and the treatment strategies recommended

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 221D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 247D1 and DENT 247D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 247D1 and DENT 247D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Periodontics
description: Introduction to the normal and disease pathways of periodontal structures with a focus on diagnosis and periodontal therapy.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 218D1/D2.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Development and Orthodontics
description: Fundamental concepts of orthodontics and development with an emphasis on psychomotor skills development are presented including management of malocclusions.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 215D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 249D1 and DENT 249D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 249D1 and DENT 249D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Clinical Care
description: Introduction to clinical care in multiple disciplines with a patient centered approach.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 224D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 250D1 and DENT 250D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 250D1 and DENT 250D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Dental Public Health
description: Oral health promotion in the community, dentist-patient relationship and communication with an emphasis on the needs of underserved populations.
notes: Students must also register for DENT 305D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 305D1 and DENT 305D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Business Aspects of Dentistry
description: Explores concepts related to the business aspects of dentistry.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 307D1 and DENT 307D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 307D1 and DENT 307D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Implantology
description: Diagnosis, treatment planning, radiographic analysis and surgical and restorative procedures to restore partial and complete edentulous spaces. Treatment of partial or complete edentulism with removable as well as fixed prostheses of either soft tissue or implant borne or partially or completely supported by titanium implants.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Practice/Junior Clerkship
description: Introduction to clinical dentistry in a multidisciplinary environment with emphasis on information gathering, diagnosis, treatment planning and acquisition of basic clinical skills.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 314.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 310J2 and DENT 310J3
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 310J1, DENT 310J2 and DENT 310J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Endodontics 1
description: Preclinical laboratory techniques on extracted and artificial teeth, rationale of endodontic therapy, anatomy, diagnosis and management of pulpal and periapical pathology including root canal preparation, obturation, periapical surgery, retropreps, apexogenesis, and trauma.
notes: Students must also register for DENT 311J2 and DENT 311J3
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 311J1, DENT 311J2 and DENT 311J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Summer Clinic Externship
description: Treatment and management of patients, including patients with handicaps.

subject: DENT
title: Community Oral Health Services 3
description: Understanding and implementing methods to reduce disparities in access to oral health care services by underserved and underprivileged people. Develop advanced understanding of the inter-relationship between oral and general health

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

notes: Students must also register for both DENT 313D1and DENT 313D2 terms
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 313D1, and DENT 313D2 are successfully completed in consecutive

subject: DENT
title: Orthodontics 1
description: Basic principles of growth and development, diagnosis, basic orthodontic techniques with clinical experience in preventive, interceptive and limited corrective treatments while assisting senior students.
notes: Students must also register for DENT 315J2 and DENT 315J3
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 315J1, DENT 315J2 and DENT 315J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry 1
description: Oral health, oral medicine, prevention, and management of oral disease including restorative procedures in children.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 316D1 and DENT 316D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 316D1 and DENT 316D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Oral Pathology and Medicine
description: The nature, identification, and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 317D1 and DENT 317D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 317D1 and DENT 317D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Periodontology
description: Examination, diagnosis, treatment planning and introduction to clinical management of periodontal diseases.
notes: Students must also register for DENT 318J2 and DENT 318J3
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 318J1, DENT 318J2 and DENT 318J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Dental Pharmacology
description: A study of the drugs that have special application to dentistry including general anaesthesia.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 319D1 and DENT 319D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 319D1 and DENT 319D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Restorative Dentistry
description: Diagnosis, treatment planning and restorative procedures to prevent deterioration of healthy teeth and to restore diseased, damaged, worn or lost teeth by means of direct and indirect operative restorations, and fixed, removable and implant prosthodontics.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 320D1/D2, DENT 321D1/D2, DENT 336D1/D2, DENT 339D1/D2.

subject: DENT
title: Image Interpretation
description: Image interpretations of various conditions affecting the head and neck region and clinical rotation in oral diagnosis and radiology.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 322.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 322J2, and DENT 322J3
No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 322J1, DENT 322J2 and DENT 322J3 are all successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
description: Diagnosis and management of the oral surgical problems encountered in general practice and exodontia clinical rotation.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Health Research 3
description: Continuation of Oral Health Research 1 and 2. Hands-on research and implementation of methodology learned in pre-requisite courses through small scale research project. Students will also work with a faculty supervisor or a graduate student mentor.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 325D1 and DENT 325D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 325D1 and DENT 325D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry Externship
description: Manage simple behavioural issues during the dental treatment of children. Recognize common dental problems in young children and recommend treatment. Provide preventive and restorative care for paediatric patients. Discuss and manage paediatric dental emergencies.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD III students during summer term only.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Decision Making A
description: Development of treatment plans for patients requiring multidisciplinary care with an emphasis on clinical decision making.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 337.

subject: DENT
title: Gerodontology
description: Principles of geriatric dentistry in an interdisciplinary care environment, including the pathology of aging, treatment plans, elder care, and critical appraisal of the most recent relevant literature topics.
notes: No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 350J1, DENT 350J2, and DENT 350J3 are successfully completed in consecutive terms
Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Decision Making
description: Development of a treatment plan for patients requiring complete mouth restoration involving multidiscipline restorative procedures with an emphasis on clinical decision making.

subject: DENT
title: Orofacial Pain and Sleep Apnea
description: Fundamental principles of orofacial pain and sleep apnea are presented, including the current evidence for diagnosis and clinical management of both conditions.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 338D1 and DENT 338D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 338D1 and DENT 338D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Endodontics B
description: Exploration of the advanced morphology, physiology and pathology of the dental pulp and periradicular tissues, including the etiology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases and injuries of the pulp and associated periradicular tissues.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taken DENT 411D1/D2.

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry B
description: Comprehensive review of the pertinent dental literature and treatment strategies in pediatric dentistry a represented with a focus on treatment planning and oral health care.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taken DENT 416D1/D2.

notes: No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 350J1, DENT 350J2, and DENT 350J3 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Patient Centred Care and Social Dentistry
description: Fundamentals of patient centred clinical approaches are presented to help dentists interact with their patients, including those with different social or cultural backgrounds.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 305D1/D2 or DENT 337.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 346D1 and DENT 346D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 346D1 and DENT 346D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Practice 1
description: Management of patient with various oral health needs involving numerous aspects of clinical dentistry.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 310J1/J2/J3.

notes: No credit will be given for this course unless DENT 350J1, DENT 350J2, and DENT 350J3 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Summer Clinic
description: This clinical oral health externship in the summer of the third year of the curriculum will focus on the management of patients with special care needs.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken DENT 312.

subject: DENT
title: Ethics and Jurisprudence
description: Law, ethical and professional issues relevant to the practice of dentistry.

restrictions.text: DMD students only.

notes: Students must also register for DENT 406D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 406D1 and DENT 406D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Practice Management
description: Management of the business of dentistry.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 405D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 407D1 and DENT 407D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 407D1 and DENT 407D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Advanced Restorative Dentistry
description: This course will focus on didactic and theoretical aspects of the clinical management of more complex restorative challenges that the senior students might expect to encounter in their final year clinical program or in private practice following graduation.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Practice/Senior Clerkship
description: Comprehensive management of patients with complex oral health needs involving all aspects of clinical dentistry.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 410D1 and DENT 410D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 410D1 and DENT 410D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Endodontics 2
description: Nickel titanium rotary endodontics, ultrasonics, electronic apex locators, problem solving canal obstruction, intracoronal bleaching, advanced anesthetic and filling techniques including management of perforations.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Orofacial Pain
description: Evaluation, diagnosis and management of common orofacial pain conditions encountered in general dentistry practice, based on current evidence-based literature. Emphasis is placed on the diagnosis and management of temporomandibular disorders with an introduction of other orofacial pain conditions.

restrictions.text: Open to D.M.D. students only.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 412D1 and DENT 412D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 412D1 and DENT 412D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Community Oral Health Services 4
description: Oral health care of the underpriviledged in outreach community locations and in the hospital environment.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

notes: Note: Participation in community clinics in the first, second and third year of the program.

subject: DENT
title: Orthodontics 2
description: Principles of growth and development, diagnosis and treatment planning, biomechanics and orthodontic techniques with clinical experience in preventive, interceptive and limited corrective treatments while mentoring junior students.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 415D1 and DENT 415D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 415D1 and DENT 415D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry 2
description: This course comprises lectures, seminars reviewing pertinent literature, and clinical treatment of children at the McCall Dental Clinic. The aim of this course is to teach the students comprehensive dental care for children.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 416D1 and DENT 416D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 416D1 and DENT 416D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Periodontology Seminar
description: Comprehensive literature review of examination, diagnosis, treatment planning and clinical management of periodontal diseases.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 418D1 and DENT 418D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 418D1 and DENT 418D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Restorative Dentistry Seminars
description: Review of recent dental literature and treatment strategies in restorative dentistry are presented, including treatment planning and digital technology.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 409.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Maxillofacial Surgery and Pathology
description: Diagnosis and management of craniofacial developmental defects, oral disease and surgical problems encountered in dentistry and emergency and exodontia clinical rotation.
notes: Students must register for both DENT 423D1 and DENT 423D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 423D1 and DENT 423D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Periodontics Clerkship
description: Understanding of the role of a Periodontist in multidisciplinary care. Recognize common periodontal conditions and recommend treatment. Providing preventative, non surgical and surgical treatment. Making recommendations for mucogingival deformities. Manage mild to moderate chronic periodontal conditions. Compose a preliminary comprehensive treatment plan in periodontics.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD IV students only.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 428D1 and DENT 428D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 428D1 and DENT 428D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: International Outreach Externship
description: Further training in operative and surgical techniques. Exposure to challenging clinical cases not normally seen in the McGill Undergraduate Teaching Clinic. Provision of care and health education to underprivileged patients with little to no access to oral health care. Exposure to diagnosis and treatment of a variety of oral infections and pathologies outside of North American context.

restrictions.text: Open to DMD students only.

notes: Students are responsible for all expenses associated with travel, accommodations, food, etc.

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Decision Making
description: Development of a treatment plan for patients requiring complete mouth restoration involving multidiscipline restorative procedures with an emphasis on clinical decision making.

subject: DENT
title: Management of Orofacial Pain
description: Principles of orofacial pain are presented, including a focus on the most current evidence for diagnosis and clinical management.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 412D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 438D1 and DENT 438D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 438D1 and DENT 438D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Endodontics C
description: Clinical endodontic management strategies, with a focus on clinical techniques and patient management.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 443D1 and DENT 443D2
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 443D1 and DENT 443D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms.

subject: DENT
title: Pediatric Dentistry C
description: Clinical pediatric management strategies, with a focus on clinical techniques and patient management.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 444D1 and DENT 444D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 444D1 and DENT 444D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Ethics and Jurisprudence A
description: Legal, ethical and professional issues relevant to the practice of dentistry.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are taking DENT 406D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 446D1 and DENT 446D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 446D1 and DENT 446D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Clinical Practice 2
description: Comprehensive management of patients with complex oral health needs, including all aspects of clinical dentistry.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences. Not open to students who have taken or are currently taking DENT 410D1/D2.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 450D1 and DENT 450D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 450D1 and DENT 450D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Focused Clinical Training
description: Comprehensive management of patients in specific dental disciplines, including complex oral health care needs.

restrictions.text: Open only to D.M.D. students in the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences.

notes: Students must register for both DENT 451D1 and DENT 451D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both DENT 451D1 and DENT 451D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: DENT
title: Biomaterials and Bioperformance
description: Biological and synthetic biomaterials, medical devices, and the issues related to their bioperformance. The physicochemical characteristics of biomaterials in relation to their biocompatibility and sterilization.

restrictions.text: Graduate and final year undergraduates from physical, biological, medical and dental sciences, and engineering.

subject: DENT
title: Epidemiology and Data Analysis in Primary Care 1
description: An introduction of epidemiological concepts, data analysis, and methods applicable to primary care research.

prerequisites.text: Permission of instructor if graduate student is outside the Faculty.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking FMED 505.

subject: DENT

subject: DENT
title: Pain Mechanisms - Cells to Organisms
description: Foundation in the basic science of pain, including cellular and molecular mechanisms, pain neuroanatomy, and key theories. Preclinical and translational pain research. Topics include: animal models of pain, peripheral and central sensitization, pain-related brain and spinal circuits, neuroimmune interactions, pain genetics, sex-dependent mechanisms, translational control of pain and new and emerging therapeutics.
notes: Basic understanding of neuroscience, cell and molecular biology are recommended

subject: DENT
title: Quantitative Data Analysis for Oral Health Research
description: A quantitative data analysis model for oral health research.

subject: DENT
title: Research Protocol Development
description: Essential skills needed to develop research proposals forclinical and population-based studies, emphasizing proposal structure, ethical considerations, feasibility, and clear presentation of research approaches and methods. Framing of research questions, selecting suitable methodological approaches, integrating ethical principles in research design, and setting realistic, feasible goals for project development within limited timeframes. Diverse research approaches and their interdisciplinary applications across health, education, and the environment.

subject: DENT
title: Evidence-Based Oral Medicine
description: Development of evidence-based decision-making, including combining the best available research data with clinical expertise and patient values.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Pharmacology Applied to Oral Medicine
description: Exploration of the pharmacological uses of drugs for commonly encountered dental conditions.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Introduction to Craniofacial Research
description: Conducting craniofacial research projects using animal models, including molecular genetics as well as methodologies commonly used in a laboratory performing craniofacial research, generating and analyzing animal models, and performing comparative studies of multiple craniofacial anomalies in humans and animal models.

restrictions.text: Registration priority will be given to students enrolled in a graduate program in Dentistry. Students from other departments may register with permission from the instructor.

subject: DENT
title: Management of Medically Complex Patients
description: Exploration of the pathophysiology of systemic diseases, including their impact on the oral cavity and/or head and neck region, how to investigate them through the medical workup, and how to modify dental treatment according to a patient's medical status.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Foundations of Mixed Methods Research
description: Basic training in how to conduct mixed methods research, the most common types of mixed methods research designs, and mixed studies reviews.

prerequisites.text: Permission of instructor if graduate student is outside the Faculty.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken or are taking FMED 614.

notes: Language of Instruction: English.

subject: DENT
title: Principles of Dental Pharmacology
description: Exploration of the basic concepts of pharmacology and pharmacotherapy as they relate to the targeted use of pharmacological drugs.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Applied Qualitative Health Research
description: Foundations of qualitative health research through consideration of theory, initiation into fieldwork and the combination of pertinent theoretical and practical components.

subject: DENT
title: Oral/Maxillofacial Radiology 1
description: General principles of radiographic indication and prescription in oral medicine, structured on the identification and analysis of all types of radiographs, including discussion of radiographic anatomy description in routine dental radiographs as well as CBCT and MRI scans. Guidance on the appropriate preliminary approach to take when a radiographic abnormality is detected.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Oral/Maxillofacial Radiology 2
description: Principles and applications of advanced imagingmodalities in dentistry, including Cone Beam ComputerTomography (CBCT) as it applies to dental decision-making, testing and diagnosis.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT

subject: DENT
title: Thesis Research 2

subject: DENT

description: Independent work under the direction of a supervisor on a research problem in the student's designated area of research.

subject: DENT
title: Thesis Research 4
description: Independent work under the direction of a supervisor on a research problem in the student's designated area of research: Data Analysis & Thesis Preparation.

subject: DENT
title: Mechanisms and Management of Pain
description: Presentation of the neurobiology of pain and analgesia, clinical pain conditions, basic and applied research methods in the study of pain, and the theory and practice of pain management. The course is designed for graduate students interested in pain mechanisms and clinical residents interested in pain management.

restrictions.text: Open to all health professionals

subject: DENT
title: General Pathology
description: Pathophysiology of disease, including the role of carcinogens and the immune system.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Principles of Health Research
description: Research topics and methodology, including critical thinking and evaluating evidence, scientific responsibilities, academic integrity, scientific writing, and publishing basics.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 563.

subject: DENT
title: Health Research Communications
description: Practical training in written and oral communication skills for biomedical sciences and oral health research.

prerequisites.text: DENT 663 or permission of the instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken DENT 564.

notes: Students will participate in a series of lectures and workshops to develop and practice scientific writing and oral communication skills.

subject: DENT
title: Leadership and Management Skills in Research
description: Introduction to leadership theory, models and practice, as well as the development of project and time management skills, resource allocation, team and consensus building.

restrictions.text: Only open to students enrolled in the MSc Dental Sciences (Thesis), MSc Dental Sciences (Non-Thesis) or the Faculty of Dentistry's PhD program, or with permission of instructor.

subject: DENT
title: Interdisciplinary/Interprofessional Approaches
description: Exploration of the links among health disciplines and health practitioners engaging in, and with, oral medicine.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Practicum Readings in Dentistry and Health Research
description: Literature that contributes general and specific practicum skills and knowledge, including a literature search, documentation of the process and preparation of the background literature for the final practicum project.

restrictions.text: Open only to students in the M.Sc. in Dental Sciences; Non-Thesis program.

subject: DENT

subject: DENT

restrictions.text: Available only to those students registered in the non-thesis option of the M.Sc. in Dental Sciences.

subject: DENT

subject: DENT
title: Biotechnology and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduction to entrepreneurship including academic discovery in biomedical sciences, to the development of intellectual property, and eventually to organization of a startup company and capitalizing on research in the biotechnology sector.

restrictions.text: Open to graduate students in medicine, surgery, biomedical sciences, engineering, science, dentistry.

notes: Note 1: Limited to 15 students. Enrollment maximum to be reviewed after 1 year.

subject: DENT
title: Orofacial Pain and Sleep Medicine
description: Development of evidence-based and patient-centred care contributing to the management of temporomandibular joint disorders, orofacial pain and sleep disorders.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Medicine/Maxillofacial Pathology 1
description: Examination of the ethology, clinical, radiographic and histologic manifestations, as well as prognosis and treatment, of specific soft tissue conditions involving the head and neck.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Oral Medicine/Maxillofacial Pathology 2
description: Review of the ethology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of oral diseases.

restrictions.text: Open only to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma in Oral Medicine.

subject: DENT
title: Readings in Dentistry and Health Research 1
description: Advanced readings in student's area of research.

restrictions.text: Open to students enrolled in a graduate program at the Faculty of Dentistry. In some circumstances, it may be opened to students from another Faculty.

subject: DENT
title: Readings in Dentistry and Health Research 2
description: Advanced readings in student's area of research.

subject: DENT
title: Readings in Dentistry and Health Research 3
description: Advanced readings in student's area of research.

restrictions.text: Open to students enrolled in a graduate program at the Faculty of Dentistry. In some circumstances, it may be opened to students from another Faculty.

subject: DENT
title: Theory of Dental Public Health
description: Theory and principles of public health, as applied to the concepts and determinants of oral health and disease, oral disease prevention and health promotion, dental care delivery systems and professional issues related to dental care delivery.

restrictions.text: Only open to graduate students enrolled in the Faculty of Dentistry

subject: DENT
title: Illness Experience and Social Determinants of Health
description: Exploration on the experience of illness and suffering, the social determinants of health, illness, access to care and broader contexts related to oral [and other] health. Critical reflection and challenge of assumptions in relation to the main themes.
notes: Priority will be given to Dentistry graduate students; other students are requested to contact the instructor with an explanation of their interest in this course.

subject: DENT
title: Bone Mechanobiology
description: Foundational theories in mechanobiology in the context of skeletal tissues (namely, bone, growth plate cartilage, and periodontal tissues). Brief introduction to structure- function relations in bone, mechanical strain, and fluid flow. Emphasis is placed on the concepts of bone adaptation to biomechanical loading patterns, mechanobiology at the tissue level and mechanotransduction at the cellular level. Research methodologies and applications to disease are discussed.

subject: DENT
title: Literature Reviews
description: Theoretical foundation and workflow outline for performing a narrative, rapid, scoping, or systematic literature review.

subject: DENT
title: Artificial Intelligence in Health and Oral Health Care
description: Fundamentals of AI and machine learning, and their application in health and oral healthcare. Exploration of how AI can support areas of care such as diagnostics, treatment planning, patient management, preventive care, and personalized interventions. Emphasis on responsible AI implementation, covering ethical, legal, social, and equity considerations in clinical practice.

subject: DENT
title: Comprehensive Exam Skills
description: Preparation for the written and oral comprehensive exam by formulating research proposals, conducting literature reviews and developing an oral presentation on the thesis topic. Emphasis will be placed on small group peer-to-peer feedback and mock examinations.

restrictions.text: Only open to students enrolled in the Faculty of Dentistry Ph.D. program.

subject: DENT
title: PhD Comprehensive Examination
description: The comprehensive exam will consist of two parts: the first part (written) will demonstrate the candidate's skills in writing a research proposal. The second part (oral) will confirm that the candidate understands all aspects of the protocol.

subject: DENT
title: Advanced Seminar in Qualitative Health Research
description: Advanced examination of qualitative research in health disciplines include an in-depth discussion of dominant qualitative research methodologies - particularly grounded theory, phenomenology/hermeneutics and ethnography - as well as a review of data collection techniques. Each qualitative methodology and technique will be examined from the perspective of a) their underlying philosophical paradigms (i.e.,epistemological and ontological premises), as well as b) their pertinence to health phenomena.

prerequisites.text: Students must have completed at least 1 qualitative research course prior to enrolling in this course AND permission of instructors.

notes: Priority will be given to Dental students enrolled in the Ad Hoc Ph.D. program.

subject: DENT
title: Foundations in Oral Health Science
description: Overview of foundational ideas in oral health science. Focus on philosophy of science (for basic science, clinical and patient care, community, population and public health). Exploration of the knowledge production cycle (e.g., from basic science to bedside care to population health, and back). Research methodologies and methods, theoretical and conceptual frameworks, knowledge translation and research ethics.

restrictions.text: Open to students enrolled in the Faculty of Dentistry's Ph.D. in Oral Health Sciences. Other students require permission of the instructors.
